How do career guides find their matches?

An official interest foundation. Full-profile career comparisons. Separate follow-ups to refine and explain possibilities.

Reviewed 17 October 2026. Comparison of the current Fieldguide source code and primary provider documentation. These are established examples, not a verified ranking by popularity. Commercial descriptions are attributed to their providers; this review did not independently validate their accuracy claims or take every live assessment end to end.

60Broad interest ratings
36Field-work ratings
17Experience, values & context screens
8–11Follow-ups per chosen pathway

113 profile screens + 9 lifestyle choices + 8 follow-ups; health has 11 follow-ups. One values screen asks for up to three of eight priorities. Exploring another field adds its follow-ups.

Interest, experience and aptitude answer different questions.

Enjoying an activity, doing it independently and demonstrating ability on a standardized task are different kinds of evidence. Our guide collects the first two; it does not measure aptitude.

Exactly how Fieldguide works today

1

Use the official Short Form

All 60 original item texts, response labels, and question sequence are preserved. Ten items contribute to each RIASEC dimension. Responses 1–5 are scored as response minus one, producing six raw totals from 0 to 40. Every answer is required; no missing value is imputed.

2

Compare the complete profile

Pearson correlation compares all six raw totals with all six direct occupational values. High and low themes both matter. Strong and very strong categories use the documented Short Form thresholds .608 and .729. These categories describe interest-pattern similarity, not career-success probabilities.

3

Group careers into pathways

A field display score averages its three closest distinct occupational profiles, where available. Fields need strong mean alignment and at least two endorsed work preferences to be featured. Conflicting fields stay available with a clear caution; there is no filler third card. Within the same category, confirmed field-work preferences and fewer concerns refine presentation, followed by correlation. This aggregation is a custom navigation rule, not a validated new scale.

4

Refine professions with tasks

All follow-ups must be answered or explicitly marked unsure. Eight task questions are standard; health adds two role-specific tasks and a separate preparation preference. Each distinct question supporting a career counts once. Suggestions need strong profile alignment and three task questions, or nonnegative overlap with six task questions, three refinements and four focused selections. Actual interest labels stay unchanged. The seven compared clinical roles also need both role-specific task choices; preparation conflict is flagged. Specific role evidence and task support come first; correlation breaks otherwise equal ties. Tied evidence is not arbitrarily cut to three, and selecting every option does not force a recommendation.

5

Handle uncertainty honestly

Incomplete profiles do not produce comparisons. Flat or weakly differentiated profiles do not produce featured matches. Close raw totals or fewer than three non-modal answers trigger a conservative custom caution. Of 117 catalog careers, 116 have direct complete occupational profiles. Tattoo work remains available without a fabricated comparison.

6

Preserve context and choice

Experience, values, education openness and Austin lifestyle do not alter official scores. Earlier custom interests, notes, completed actions and plans stay saved. Students answer the new official items themselves; old answers are never relabeled. An explicit career choice remains possible even when the interest pattern differs.

What changed about question order?

The official Short Form retains its original sequence. Our separate field-work prompts mix twelve fields in balanced twelve-question blocks. Experience questions stay together with the same four response choices. Values and work preferences have separate sections. The order is saved for Back, reload and resume; earlier custom answers remain saved separately. Answers stay attached to question IDs. The new official questions require fresh answers. Their wording and labels are preserved; our technical presentation and combined guidance still need student testing.

What we should improve next

  1. Study comprehension, completion burden, stability and usefulness with actual high-school students. Published evidence for the official instrument does not establish validity of our complete application.
  2. Test whether our custom field and task follow-ups add useful discrimination beyond the official interest profile. Keep counselor review and student experiences in the evaluation.
  3. Keep interest alignment, experience, values, training requirements and lifestyle feasibility visibly separate. Avoid a single percentage implying a probability of success.
  4. Evaluate with actual high-school students: comprehension, completion burden, repeatability, sensitivity to order, and agreement with unmodified established tools. Agreement alone is not predictive validation.
  5. Use a properly administered external performance assessment when measured aptitude is needed. Four-choice experience answers cannot supply that measurement.
